title: What electricians do
d: Electricians install, maintain, and repair the wiring, panels, and devices that power buildings. It is a licensed trade learned through 4-5 year apprenticeships
description: Electricians install, maintain, and repair the wiring, panels, and devices that power buildings. It is a licensed trade learned through 4-5 year apprenticeships. Work splits into residential, commercial, and industrial — each with its own code articles and skills.

title: Essential tools
d: Non-contact voltage tester, multimeter, insulated screwdrivers, wire strippers, lineman's pliers, needle-nose pliers, fish tape, cable ripper, level, headlamp,
description: Non-contact voltage tester, multimeter, insulated screwdrivers, wire strippers, lineman's pliers, needle-nose pliers, fish tape, cable ripper, level, headlamp, and a sturdy tool bag. Pros add: circuit tracer, clamp meter, knockout set, and thermal camera.

title: Key skills
d: Reading blueprints and one-line diagrams, bending conduit (EMT), pulling wire, making up panels neatly, troubleshooting with meters, and knowing the NEC code co
description: Reading blueprints and one-line diagrams, bending conduit (EMT), pulling wire, making up panels neatly, troubleshooting with meters, and knowing the NEC code cold. Troubleshooting is the highest-paid skill: half the job is finding the fault.

title: Safety essentials
d: Test before you touch — every time, even if you turned it off. Lockout/tagout on commercial jobs. One hand in the panel when possible. Arc-flash awareness: neve
description: Test before you touch — every time, even if you turned it off. Lockout/tagout on commercial jobs. One hand in the panel when possible. Arc-flash awareness: never work live above your training. Ladders fiberglass, not aluminum.

title: Pro tips
d: Label everything as you go. Take panel photos before touching. Torque lugs to spec — loose connections start fires. Keep wire nuts and staples organized. Never
description: Label everything as you go. Take panel photos before touching. Torque lugs to spec — loose connections start fires. Keep wire nuts and staples organized. Never bury a junction box behind drywall; it is a code violation and a future nightmare.
